## Close evidence — change merged, all six ACs discharged

Gerrit **2689** submitted; commit **`1f7673cb2c53`** ("Gzip the user-data so terraform can plan again") carries `rebar-ticket: a68c-9633-248c-4b06` and is current `origin/main` HEAD. Verified as an ancestor of the worktree the close runs from (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` → OK).

AC-by-AC, against evidence already recorded on this ticket and re-verified in the tree at `1f7673cb2c53`:

| AC | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 plan GENERATES | MET | RED at `84ef284833be` was rc=1 with one `Error:` (the length rejection); after the change **rc=2**, zero `Error:` lines |
| AC2 no replacement | MET | `aws_instance.gerrit will be updated in-place`; `Plan: 2 to add, 25 to change, 0 to destroy`; grep for `forces replacement\|must be replaced\|will be destroyed` → **0**. Read from plan output, not from the provider default, as the AC demands |
| AC3a payload decodes to the intended script | MET | 9,256 b64 chars → 6,941 gzip bytes → 16,668 decompressed; `1f 8b` magic; diff vs `templatefile()` render = 9 hunks, being exactly the 3 declared interpolations + 7 `$${`→`${` un-escapings — the only differences the AC permits |
| AC3b cloud-init acceptance deferred with a back-out | MET **as written** | The AC requires the acceptance be *explicitly deferred with a back-out*, not proven. Its in-session half is discharged (AC3a + the magic bytes cloud-init dispatches on). See the operator note below |
| AC4 guard measures rendered-then-encoded | MET | `scripts/check_user_data_size.py` invoked at **`Makefile:411`** inside the `lint:` target. Run: `rendered 16920 B, transported 7100 B (gzipped), limit 16384 — 9284 bytes of headroom (43% used)`, rc=0, no AWS calls (hermetic, so portable to any CI provider or none). Oracle `tests/unit/test_user_data_size_a68c.py`: **14 passed**, including both defect seeds (`drop-gzip`, `regrow-script`) proving the guard is load-bearing rather than decorative |
| AC5 drift branches on `-detailed-exitcode` | MET | `.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml:139-176` — `case "$rc"` → 0 "drift: NONE", 2 "drift: DETECTED", `*` "**PLAN COULD NOT BE GENERATED (exit $rc) — this is NOT drift**", then `exit "$rc"`, so **both** non-zero outcomes stay hard failures. No second detection mechanism added |
| AC6 09-03/09-04 drift failures explained | MET | 09-03 run 33724312912 exit **2** = genuine unapplied drift; 09-04 run 33845247102 exit **3** = `terraform fmt -check` on `monitoring_9ea3.tf` aborting before plan (bug `fd2b-7af3`, since fixed — `fmt` is now its own job with no `needs:` on `plan`); 09-05 run 33950205876 exit 1 = this bug. Each read from `gh run view --log-failed` |

### Still owed by an operator (does not block this close)

**AC3b's discharge condition.** The instance is *updated in place*, so the new payload does not execute until a future **launch** — cloud-init runs user-data once per instance, and a mere reboot re-executes it under neither encoding, so there is no exposure in the meantime. At the next launch, confirm `user_data.sh complete.` in `/var/log/cloud-init-output.log`. **If that confirmation fails**, the back-out order written into AC3b applies: (1) recover on the box — `curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/user-data | gunzip | bash` re-runs the identical script, since IMDS returns the already-base64-decoded gzip bytes; (2) durably, switch to the S3-bootstrap alternative (a small **plaintext** user_data that fetches the script). Reverting to the previous plaintext `user_data` is **not** a back-out and must not be attempted — that is the 16,668-byte payload this ticket exists to fix, and it cannot be planned at all.

### Two residuals, neither an AC, both deliberately out of scope

1. The guard compares **decoded gzip bytes** against 16,384 and does not additionally cap the base64 *string*. If the provider caps both, there is an unreachable band (gzip 12,288–16,384 B). Current payload is 7,100 B — **5,188 B below that band's floor** — so it is not reachable today. Worth a two-line hardening later.
2. The drift **backlog** itself (`2 to add, 25 to change`) is real and unapplied. That is an operator `terraform apply`, not this ticket.

Closing `preexisting`: this was an omission that accumulated over ~ten weeks as the file grew, with `0033662b5534` the commit that crossed the limit — not a regression introduced by a specific change.
